ai_playground_model_usage

This table records the usage count of different AI models in the AI Playground. Usage is tracked per user and per model; that is, each user has a separate count for each model. The usage count is used to enforce quotas and is reset daily by a scheduled job.

Foreign key constraints

Column name Data type Default value Value constraint Default constraint Identity? Nullable? Description
pk1 id true false

Surrogate primary key. Uniqueness of records is enforced by users_pk1 and model_name.
users_pk1 id false false

Foreign key to users.pk1.
model_name int 0 false false

AI model for which usage count and quota are tracked, e.g. AMAZON_NOVA_MICRO, AMAZON_NOVA_LITE. This is represented as an int for easier querying and indexing, and the mapping of int to model name is maintained in the application code. The default 0 denotes None for backward compatibility.
usage_count int 1 false false

The number of times the user has used the model in the AI Playground. This count is used to enforce usage quotas.

activity_accumulator

This is the table that tracks user activity. Almost every page a user visits in your system gets recorded here. It is like your apache access logs but with better user tracking.

Primary key constraint

activity_accumulator_pk

  • pk1

Indexes

  1. activity_accumulator_ie2
    • timestamp
  2. activity_accumulator_ie3
    • user_pk1
  3. activity_accumulator_ie4
    • course_pk1
  4. activity_accumulator_ie5
    • forum_pk1
  5. activity_accumulator_ie6
    • session_id
  6. activity_accumulator_icontent
    • content_pk1
  7. activity_accumulator_ie7
    • event_type
    • timestamp
Column name Data type Default value Value constraint Default constraint Identity? Nullable? Description
pk1 bigid true false

This is the surrogate primary key for the table.
event_type varchar(30) false false

This is the type of activity. Groups the event based on what occurred. For example, TAB_ACCESS (page view), PAGE_ACCESS (page view, Triggered when a page, other than a course, organization, content, module, or tab is accessed on the system. The name of the navigation item will be returned.), LOGIN_ATTEMPT, LOGOUT, SESSION_TIMEOUT, COURSE_ACCESS (Page view, Triggered when a course frameset is loaded, or when a page is accessed in a course. The name of the navigation item will be returned.), SESSION_INT (Triggered when a session is initialized), etc. The full list of values is in the TrackingEvent.Type enumueration.
user_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].users table to indicate the owner of the activity. This can be NULL if the user cannot be determined. If the user has logged in, then there activity is tied to their user_pk1.
course_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign ley referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].course_main table to indicate the Course the activity is occuring in. This will be NULL if the activity occurs outside a Course. If the user has logged in, then there activity is tied to their user_pk1.
group_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the group table to indicate the Course Group this activity belongs to. This will be NULL if the activity is not Course Group related.
forum_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the forum table to indicate the Forum this activity is taking place in. Forum activity can take place within a Course or Institution Discussion Board. This will be NULL if the activity takes place outside a Forum.
internal_handle varchar(255) false true

This is a foreign key referencing the internal_handle column of the [AS_CORE].navigation_item table. This is tracked whenever a user accesses a page in the the Academic Suite (eg. When either a PAGE_ACCESS or COURSE_ACCESS event occurs). This will be NULL for events other than PAGE_ACCESS and COURSE_ACCESS. Internal system identifier for the event. This field corresponds to the unique ID in the NAVIGATION_ITEM table. Not all page requests correspond to a navigation item, so this field may often appear blank. If this field is empty, check the CONTENT_PK1 field. If the page accessed displayed content, the primary key for the piece of content will appear in that field.
content_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table to indicate the Course Content this activity is associated with. This will be NULL if the activity is not Course Content related. If the user has logged in, then there activity is tied to their user_pk1. This field is populated when the EVENT_TYPE is CONTENT_ACCESS.
data nvarchar(255) false true

This contains any free-form text data associated with the event. Data related to the event. This field provides additional information on the event. Each event uses this field, if at all, in different ways. In many instances, the data included in this field is a value that is easily deduced. In some instances, the value in the data field is a number, such as _1_1 or _29_1. These are associated with an EVENT_TYPE of TAB_ACCESS. The first number is an ID that references a tab or a module (the second number can be ignored). The ID number that refers to a tab can be found in the user interface by scrolling over the tab. The ID number appears as part of the URL in the status bar.The ID number that refers to a module can be found in the same manner. Scroll over the Maximize, Minimize, or Edit button associated with a module. The ID number will appear as part of the URL in the status bar. Please note that the Detach Module button returns a different ID number and should be ignored.
timestamp datetime NOW false true

This is the date and/or time at which this event occurred.
status numeric false true

This indicates the status of the event. Value values are success (1) or failure (0). The values come from the TrackingEvent.Status enumeration.
session_id id false true

This is a reference to the primary key of the user session associated with this activity. Identifies the user session that initiated the action. A session is simply a browser connection to the system launched from an end-user machine.
ip_address ipaddress false true

IP address from which the event was generated (optional).

    Default On. The tool will be enabled by default in newly-created courses.

  • F

 false true

  • F

    Default Off. The tool will be disabled by default in newly-created organizations.

  • A

    Always On. The tool will be enabled in all organizations, and cannot be disabled.

 false true

If the tool is enabled (via the enabled_mask column), this column determines the enablement status at the organization level.

This the localized description of the tool (almost always a bundle key reference).

This is the bit mask that indicates if guest is allowed to use this tool. SYSTEM = 0x00000001, COURSE = 0x00000002, ORG = 0x00000004, COURSE_GROUP = 0x00000008, ORG_GROUP = 0x00000010, NAVITEM_COURSE = 0x00000001, NAVITEM_ORG = 0x00000002, NONE = 0x00000000, ALL = 0xffffffff.

attribute_definition

An AttributeDefinition contains the meta-data describing an attribute of an entity within the system. These attributes can be user-defined or system attributes. The template and form framework uses these definitions to map fields to their attributes, and the persistence system uses these definitions to determine where to load and store an entity's attribute values.

attribute_list_column_set

This table represents a collection of active list columns. Active columns are the subset of available columns that are displayed in a particular column configuration. There are two kinds of lists. System Default is the default set of columns at the entity type level. All lists that belong to this type and do not exist in an operating unit context will use this set as their default. Customized is the set of columns that has been customized by a user, at either the system or ou-level (operating unit level).

is_locale_enforced char(1) false true

Values:Y/N: If Y then the locale will be forced to locale regardless of what the user's personal preferences have set for their locale
asmt_upgrade_version numeric 0 false false

The assessment data has to go through a number of runtime upgrade steps before assessments are usable in a course. This field records the current upgrade-state of the assessments data within this course.
asmt_upgrade_flags numeric 0 false false

After any import or restore operation the asmt_upgrade_version is set back to 0 and any new data re-upgraded. There are certain parts of the upgrade which do not have to run in this case (i.e. the upgrade is only required once per course, not after each import operation). This field is used to store those flags to avoid re-running pieces of the upgrade
honor_term_avail_ind char(1) 'N' course_main_hnr_trm_av_ck
  • Y
  • N
false true

if Y then use the term for available_ind; if N then use those fields from this table. (Note that duration implicitly affects availability through fields such as startdate and enddate but those are only controlled by the term when course.duration=T)
course_theme_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].course_theme table. It is the course theme that is used for the course.
import_task_pk1 id false true

The latest queued task pk1 which is import/restore/copy into this course. it is overwritten if multiple ones are queued. This field is transient so not be included in course copy or content exchange operations
uuid nvarchar(32) false true

A unique (generated) identifier for this course. Sent as the context_id in LTI launch requests.
copy_from_uuids varchar(329) false true

The source course uuid(s) on copy. This could be a comma-separated list. Sent as the context_id_history in LTI launch requests. Configured to hold up to 10.
course_view_option char(1) course_main_ck1
  • I

    Instructors can choose course view at anytime

  • U

    The course will use Ultra view, instructors can't change it

  • C

    The course will use Original view, instructors can't change it

 false true

This is course view option flag. It's different from ultra_status flag, this flag control if instructor can change the course view or change directly by admin, while ultra_status just indicate the current course view of this course is. Also, if the course ultra_status is in ULTRA_DECIDED state, then this flag will be ignored. If null, then the default value depends on the system-wide ultra setting: If ultra is ON then null is effectively 'I' If ultra is OFF then null is effectively 'C'

ultra_status char(1) ultra_status_enum
  • N

    No explicit decision has been made yet (for now treated the same as classic-decided)

  • C

    The classic user experience has explicitly been chosen

  • U

    The Ultra user experience has explicitly been chosen.

  • P

    The course is currently an Ultra course but in preview mode.

 false true

This is the flag indicating if the course is classic, ultra, or ultra preview. Note that updates to this field are controlled in java code so please do not blindly change it directly. Specifically you can only perform these transitions: N->C, N->U, N->P, C->U, C->P, P->U, P->C, U->NOTHING. You cannot go back once you pick U The NULL value, which represents classic, will be left for all the legacy courses and treated the same as classic

is_closed_ind char(1) course_main_is_closed_ck
  • Y

    the course is closed for student access

  • N

    the student is able to access the course

 false true

This is the flag indicating if the course is closed for student access. Even if the course is closed, the course is still listed in the student's course listing. The NULL value will be interpreted as N

convert_task_pk1 id false true

The latest queued task pk1 which is a course conversion. it is overwritten if multiple ones are queued. This field is transient so not be included in course copy or content exchange operations
ultra_conversion_report_id id false true

The identifier for the conversion report when the course was converted from original to Ultra. This field is transient so not be included in content exchange operations
owner char(1) course_main_owner_ck
  • L

    Learn

  • F

 false true

Indicates which system is the source of truth for the record. Defaults to Learn if unset.

The ID of this course in Foundations

  • N

    Progress tracking is disabled for the course, and enabling it will require data migration. New Ultra courses should use the 'O' indicator

  • O

This column is used by the Ultra UI to determinate whether the current user has time limit accommodation A null value means not set time limit accommodation as default. event_prop

A child table to the event table. This tracks the details of an object modification such as the object property that was updated, and its old and new values. For example, if a user record's address property was modified and tracked via a corresponding modification event record, an entry in this table would contain the address as the property and the old and new addresses as the old and new values.

time_limit int false true

This is the assessment time limit for completion in minutes.
soft_time_limit int false true

Unit in minutes. In the case of tests with a (time_limit), if this is null then it means there is no soft-time-limit and behaves same as Learn 9.1. If it's not null, user will receive an alert if the (soft_time_limit) expires. Depending on the value of (timer_completion), user will be forced to submit attempt ((timer_completion) is (H)) or be alerted again but can continue working without deadline ((timer_completion) is (C)) if the (time_limit) expires then. So (soft_time_limit) should be always less than (time_limit) if it's not null, this will be ensured and checked at REST API level.

show_inst_description_ind char(1) false true

This boolean flag (Y/N) indicates whether the instructor provided description is displayed on the begin-test page before you actually start the test.
allow_late_submission_ind char(1) false true

This boolean flag (Y/N) indicates whether late attempts can't be created after the due date. If set to 'Y' students won't be allowed to start an assessment after the due date.
feedback_settings varchar(255) false true

Pipe (|) separated list of enabled student feedback options. List item are of the form -> state:feedbackOption1,feedbackOption2. Possible states are: as(After Submission), ashr(After submission, then hide results), osd(On Specific Date), add(After Due Date), aaed(After Availability End Date), aas(After Attempts are submitted), aag(After Attempts are graded), aiag(After individual grade is posted). Possible feedback options are: s(score), ua(useranswer), ca(correct), f(feedback), aa(allanswers), ia(incorrect).

qti_block_mapping

Each question-block is a single row in qti_asi_data where the qti xml contains a list of all the questions it references. This qti_block_mapping reflects that relationship of 1 question block and n questions This table is actually dual-purpose, also supporting random blocks. Each random-block is a single row in qti_asi_data. Historically a random block had a single source pool stored both in the qti xml and in objectbank_pk1. With the support of multiple source pools for a random block, this table augments that column which is being left in the db to avoid any upgrade-time overhead. When used for random blocks we reflect the following relationship. 1 random block and n pools. It is 'ok' to re-use this table because it is modeling a 1 qti_asi_data_pk1 and n qti_asi_data_pk1 style of relationship in both cases.

Primary key constraint

qti_block_mapping_pk

  • pk1

Foreign key constraints

  1. qti_blck_mppng_qustn_blck_fk1 (On Delete Cascade)
    • question_block_pk1
  2. qti_blck_mppng_qstn_fk2
    • question_pk1

Indexes

  1. qti_block_mapping_if1
    • question_block_pk1
  2. qti_block_mapping_if2
    • question_pk1

pk1 id true false

This table really doesn't need a pk1 at all, but our framework dao code likes it when there is a pk1

FK to qti_asi_data for the question block or random block being dealt with. When the question-block or random block qti is deleted, all matching rows in this table will be deleted through a cascade-delete constraint
question_pk1 id false false

FK to qti_asi_data if for a question block, for each question in the block; if for a random block, for each referenced source pool in the block. Deletion of the question (question block case) or pool (random block case) will fail due to this constraint because java code has to be used to remove the reference from the question blocks QTI xml

multiple_attempts_ind char(1) false true

This boolean flag (Y/N/null) indicates if the assessment can be attempted multiple times, null means no exception setting for this field.
unlimited_attempts_ind char(1) false true

This boolean flag (Y/N/null) indicates if the assessment can be attempted unlimited times when multiple_attempts_ind sets to Y. N when multiple_attempts_ind is set to Y would indicate that the assessment is allowed for multiple attempts for the number of times set by attempt_count, null means no exception setting for this field.
attempt_count int false true

This is the number of attempts allowed when multiple_attempts_ind is set to Y and unlimited_attempts_ind to N, null means no exception setting for this field.
force_completion_ind char(1) false true

This boolean flag (Y/N/null) indicates if the assessment must be completed the first time it is launched, null means no exception setting for this field.
timer_completion char(1) false true

This is the enum value to show Continual (C) or Hardstop (H), null means no exception setting for this field.
time_limit int false true

This is the assessment time limit for completion in minutes.
soft_time_limit int false true

Unit in minutes. In the case of tests with a (time_limit), if this is null then it means there is no soft-time-limit and behaves same as Learn 9.1. If it's not null, user will receive an alert if the (soft_time_limit) expires. Depending on the value of (timer_completion), user will be forced to submit attempt ((timer_completion) is (H)) or be alerted again but can continue working without deadline ((timer_completion) is (C)) if the (time_limit) expires then. So (soft_time_limit) should be always less than (time_limit) if it's not null, this will be ensured and checked at REST API level.
ipfilter_ind char(1) 'N' indicator_uto5

  • N
false false

This boolean flag (Y/N) indicates whether this test deployment is restricted by IP address.

blog_stream_event

Stores blog or journal related stream events to populate the My Blackboard stream viewer

Primary key constraint

blog_stream_event_pk

This is the name of primary key constraint

  • pk1

Foreign key constraints

  1. blog_stream_event_fk1 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the blog table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • blog_pk1
  2. blog_stream_event_fk2 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the blog_comment table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • blog_comment_pk1
  3. blog_stream_event_fk3 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the blog_entry table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • blog_entry_pk1
  4. blog_stream_event_fk4 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the users table, referential action cascade on delete (cascade).

    • actor_pk1
  5. blog_stream_event_fk5 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the users table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • actee_pk1
  6. blog_stream_event_fk6 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_main table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • crsmain_pk1
  7. blog_stream_event_fk7 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the groups table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • group_pk1
  8. blog_stream_event_fk8 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • course_contents_pk1
  9. blog_stream_event_fk9 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_users table, referential action cascade on delete (setnull).

    • creator_course_users_pk1

Column name Data type Default value Value constraint Default constraint Identity? Nullable? Description
pk1 id true false

This is the surrogate primary key for the table.
actor_pk1 id false true

FK to users.pk1 for the person doing the action - i.e. a comment on a blog would set the commenter in actor_pk1. This column will be set to NULL if the user was deleted in which case this row should be ignored.
actee_pk1 id false true

FK to users.pk1 for the person the action was done against - i.e. a comment on a blog entry would set the post-author in actee_pk1. This will be NULL if the stream event is not in response to a particular user or if the user was deleted.
crsmain_pk1 id false true

FK to course_main for the course in which the event occurs. Will be set to NULL if the course was deleted.
group_pk1 id false true

FK to groups for the group in which the event occurs. This will be NULL for non group blogs/journals or if the group was deleted.
event_date datetime false false

Date and time the event occurred.
event_modified_date datetime false false

Date and time the event was modified (only set in response to a cascade setnull trigger - see FKs below).
course_contents_pk1 id false true

FK to course_contents.pk1 if the event pertains to a course contents item. This will be NULL if the event does not have a course_contents.pk1 or if the course content was deleted.
journal_ind char(1) 'N' false false

This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if this is a blog or a journal (Y== Journal))
event_type varchar(2) blog_stream_event_type_ck
  • EP

    Blog or Journal entry posted event

  • EE

    Blog entry edited event

  • CP

    Blog or Journal comment posted event

 false false

The type of event such as: entry, edit or comment post.
event_text nvarchar(333) false true

Text specific to this event - not the stream text directly, but the dynamic text to substitute into an event-appropriate message when rendering the stream.
event_title nvarchar(333) false true

Title for the stream event
blog_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the blogs table. One and only one of blog_pk1, blog_comment_pk1 or blog_entry_pk1 should be specified. If all 3 are NULL the row should be ignored
blog_comment_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the blog_comment table. One and only one of blog_pk1, blog_comment_pk1 or blog_entry_pk1 should be specified. Is set to NULL if the associated blog comment is deleted. If all 3 are NULL the row should be ignored
blog_entry_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the blog_entry table. One and only one of blog_pk1, blog_comment_pk1 or blog_entry_pk1 should be specified. Is set to NULL if the associated entry is deleted. If all 3 are NULL the row should be ignored
creator_course_users_pk1 id false true

FK to course_users.pk1 for the course membership of the user who is the original author of the blog entry. This column will be set to NULL if the membership was deleted or the blog entry is set as anonymous.

blti_provider_cred

This table contains the most recent secret associated with a provider key and host, used in performing a Basic LTI launch. Credentials in this table are generated during a Basic LTI launch, if credential caching is enabled for the launch and the calling code has one or more of the permissions advertised via the blackboard.platform.callbackRequiredPermissions extension-point. See the documentation in the interface blackboard.platform.blti.CallbackRequiredPermissions for more details.

Column name Data type Default value Value constraint Default constraint Identity? Nullable? Description
pk1 id true false

This is the surrogate primary key for the table.
actor_pk1 id false true

FK to users.pk1 for the person doing the action - i.e. a comment on a post would set the commenter in actor_pk1. This column will be set to NULL if the user was deleted in which case this row should be ignored.
actee_pk1 id false true

FK to users.pk1 for the person the action was done against - i.e. a comment on a post would set the post-author in actee_pk1. This will be NULL if the stream event is not in response to a particular user or if the user was deleted.
crsmain_pk1 id false true

FK to course_main for the course in which the event occurs. This will be NULL if the stream event occurs within a community discussion board or if the course was deleted.
group_pk1 id false true

FK to groups for the group in which the event occurs. This will be NULL for non group discussion boards or if the group was deleted.
event_date datetime false false

Date and time the event occurred.
event_modified_date datetime false false

Date and time the event was modified (only set in response to a cascade setnull trigger - see FKs below).
course_contents_pk1 id false true

FK to course_contents.pk1 if the event pertains to a course contents item. This will be NULL if the event does not have a course_contents.pk1 or if the course content was deleted.
ultra_group_forum_contents_pk1 id false true

FK to course_contents.pk1 if the event is fired in a group discussion (real forum). This will be NULL if the forum related to this event is not group disscussion. This column is only used for group discussions in an Ultra course.

  • FC

  • FS

  • FU

  • TS

    Thread subscribed event

  • TU

    Thread unsubscribed event

 false false

The event type identifier constrained to the below values.
event_text nvarchar(333) false true

Text specific to this event - not the stream text directly, but the dynamic text to substitute into an event-appropriate message when rendering the stream.
thread_subject nvarchar(300) false true

This is the thread subject as of the time when the message was first posted. AB#506329: A task was created to update this value if it ever changes.
forum_main_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the forum_main table. This column will be set to NULL if the forum was deleted in which case this row will be ignored for new events and otherwise used to purge existing events from the UI
msg_main_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the msg_main table. This column will be set to null if the msg was deleted in which case the row will be ignored for new events and otherwise used to purge existing events from the UI
parent_msg_main_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the msg_main table for the parent thread message.
non_group_thread_msg_main_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the msg_main table for the top thread message that is not associated to a group. This applies only to ULTRA and is used to manage discussion subscription.
top_level_response_users_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the users table for the actor of the top level response of the message.
actor_acts_as_instructor_ind char(1) 'N' indicator_actor_acts_as_instructor
  • Y
  • N
false true

This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating if the actor of the message acts as an instructor.
highlight_ind char(1) 'N' indicator_highlight
  • Y
  • N
false true

This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating if the user name should be highlighted in the stream as moderator or manager. An extra check is done in the java code to check if it still should be highlighted.
indirect_ind char(1) indicator_dse_indirect
  • Y
  • N
false true

This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating if the discussion is within the INDIRECT content area (In Ultra courses an INDIRECT courseToc is created which is not 'visible' to the users in the UI. Things like conversations-on-content are created within this folder as a forum link but need to be presented differently in the stream - as a conversation and not a discussion)

This is mapped to er_item_set_item (as opposed to er_item) because a user can manually remove an item from the evidence set (when an item is removed from an evidence set it is not removed from the repository itself). Besides, we care how an item made it into an evidence set, not how it made it into the repository.

gradebook_main

This represents a Gradable Item (and a Column in the Grade Center). Gradebook Main describes a column in the gradebook. Every gradebook column gets a row in this table. delta_due_date int false true

Indicates whether the user or group has a due date exception. A value equal to zero means the item will never be marked as late, and a value not equal to zero means the new due date is the gradable item's due date plus this value, which specifies a duration in minutes (can be positive or negative). If this value and fixed_due_date are both null, then there is no due date exception. Both cannot be simultaneously non-null.
fixed_due_date datetime false true

Indicates whether the user or group has a due date exception. A non-null value represents the new due date for this user/group's gradable item. If this value and delta_due_date are both null, then there is no due date exception. Both cannot be simultaneously non-null.
due_date_exception_type char(1) 'N' due_date_exception_type_enum
  • N

    Normal: No due date exception (delta_due_date and fixed_due_date are both null).

  • F

    Fixed: Due date exception is static or fixed (fixed_due_date is non-null).

  • R

    Relative: Due date exception is relative to the gradable item's due date (delta_due_date is non-null and non-zero).

  • U

    Unlimited: No due date; the item should never be marked as late (delta_due_date is zero).

 false false

The type of the due date exception.
date_added datetime false false

This is the date and/or time at which this event occurred.
date_modified datetime false true

This is the date and/or time at which this event modified.

This column defines the type of scale in use. The possible values are below: 1. T -- Translation, meaning the grade displayed is between a range of possible values, and is calculated using a defined value 2. S -- Score, the value shown is the points awarded the student out of the total points possible 3. X -- Text, the value shown is in plain text, where the entry begins with a number, which is calculated as a Score (S) 4. P -- Percentage, the value shown is the percent out of 100 that the student received 5. C -- Complete/Incomplete, the value shown has two possible values, complete (C) and incomplete (I)

This table lists sets of standards from each standards provider. Some standards providers publish multiple sets of standards documents that each cover all disciplines. For example a state might publish a set of "Assessment Standards" and another set of "Curriculum Standards". Typically each set will contain standard documents for the full set of disciplines that that state releases standards for. In cases where a standards provider does not publish multiple sets of documents, a placeholder record is created in this table to contain all of that state's standards documents.

This is the surrogate primary key for the table.
parent_id nvarchar(255) false true

This is the identifier of the parent item. If this notification is conceptually subordinate to another notifications - as Assignment Submitted is subordinate to Assignment Due, for example - then this column contains the id of the parent notification.

dtcreated datetime NOW false false

This is the date and/or time at which this event occurred. The date on which the item was first added.

title nvarchar(333) false false

This is the title of the notification item. This will be visible to the user in the UI.
crsmain_pk1 id false false

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_main table.
owner_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the users table. A foreign key reference to the user who created this item, or is responsible for it.

source_id nvarchar(255) false false

This is the source or content item that originated this notification item. An identifier that uniquely specifies the item on which we're notifying. It's the responsibility of the individual subsystems to ensure that this uniqueness.

crs_contents_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table. This represents the content item from the course or organization that originated this notification. This will be populated when the notification is generated by content, otherwise null.
parent_content_pk1 id false true

This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the course_contents table. This represents the parent of the content item that originated this notification.
source_type char(2) false false

This is the source type of the notification item. The class of event this represents: an assignment event, or an assessment event, or a content event, etc

event_type nvarchar(255) false true

This is the type of event for this notification item, ie. AVAILABLE or OVERDUE. The specifi A=c type of event, within the course_type, that this represent: Assignment Available, or example, or Assignment Submitted S=Scheduled; A= Available.
type char(1) 'S' eud_item_type
  • S

    This represents Scheduled.

  • A

    This represents Available.

 false false

This is the type of notification item. Whether this is a Scheduled or an Available notification. S=Scheduled; A=Available.
start_date datetime nowTx false false

The time when the action happened. The date on which the notification period should begin - which usually maps to the date on which the item will become available. If this is specified, we won't display notification until this date is reached. Note that this is not related to adaptive release rules - those will be evaluated separately and independently.

due_date datetime false true

This is the due date associated with the source that originated this notification. The date on which this notification is due. Internally, the due date is used to figure out when to send reminders, and also to determine whether transform DUE events into OVERDUE events.

secondary_date datetime false true

This is an additional date associated with the source that originated this notification. This value is informational display data and is not used for notification scheduling.
end_date datetime false true

The time when the action ended. The date on which the notification period should end - which usually maps to the date on which the item will become unavailable. If this is specified, we won't display notification after this date is reached. Note that this is not related to adaptive release rules - those will be evaluated separately and independently.

data_pending_ind char(1) 'N' eud_data_pending_at_create_ind
  • Y
  • N
false false

Whether this notification is in the midst of being created - ie, whether it is waiting for its associated recipients to be created. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification is in the midst of being created - ie, whether it is waiting for its associated recipients to be created.
can_replace_ind char(1) 'Y' eud_can_replace_ind
  • Y
  • N
false false

Whether this notification can be replaced by incoming notifications that would normally obviate them. See Notification Replacement for more details. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification can be replaced by incoming notifications that would normally obviate them.
important_ind char(1) 'N' eud_important
  • Y
  • N
false false

This is, unfortunately, a very nebulous name for a very specific concept. An important marker indicates that, during a blitz (which is to say, a mass notification) this notification should always be sent out to its recipients, no matter what. See Notification Blitz for more details. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification item is important.
semi_important_ind char(1) 'N' eud_semi_important
  • Y
  • N
false false

An semi-important marker indicates that notifications will be treated as important for new enrolled users prior to the start date, so that notification can be sent out to those new enrolled users. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification item is semi-important.
override_setting_ind char(1) 'N' eud_override_stng_ind
  • Y
  • N
false false

Whether this notification should ignore any system/user customizations that would normally suppress its dissemination. This is useful for notifications that absolutely, positively must get out there. This is a boolean flag (Y/N) indicating whether this notification item should be delivered to recipients regardless of their individual notification settings.
default_receiver_status char(1) 'U' eud_receiver_status
  • U

    Unprocessed. Waiting for distribution.

  • N

    Notified. Has been disseminated to all distributors.

  • F

    Failed. Distribution failed for all distributors.

  • D

  • Z

    Neuter. Never intended to be distributed.

 false false

This represents the status of the default receiver.
default_sender_status char(1) 'U' eud_sender_status

 false false

force_notify_ind char(1) 'N' eud_force_notify_ind

false false

This is a boolean flag (Y/N) that indicates if the notification should be forced to be sent regardless the course status.

Home > video-integration_b2

content_owner

This table contains FKs to entities that can have VTBE/BbML associated with them. At most one FK may be non-null. When bulk delete ocurrs, such as when a course is deleted or when an attempt is deleted, the FK is set to null, and will be cleaned up in a different thread. So the state where all FKs, crsmain_pk1 excluded, are null is very short-lived and is required so that cleanup work which can caused delays is done asynchronously. As new entities are added which can have VTBE/BbML associated to them, a new FK column is added to this table. Note: This table allows tools with 1 or more VTBE fields to register as a content owner so that they can be associated generically to other objects in the database. As such, the table is not video integration specific and can be moved to core in the future.

Primary key constraint

content_owner_pk

This is the name of primary key constraint on column pk1.

Foreign key constraints

    • crsmain_pk1
  2. content_owner_fk2 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].attempt table. No cascade delete because cleanup for associated data needs to be handled in the code.

    • attempt_pk1
  3. content_owner_fk3 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].group_attempt table. No cascade delete because cleanup for associated data needs to be handled in the code.

    • group_attempt_pk1
  4. content_owner_fk4 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].attempt_staged_grading table. No cascade delete because cleanup for associated data needs to be handled in the code.

    • attempt_staged_grading_pk1
  5. content_owner_fk5 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].group_attempt_staged_grading table. No cascade delete because cleanup for associated data needs to be handled in the code.

    • grp_att_staged_grading_pk1
  6. content_owner_fk6 (On Delete SetNull)

    This is a foreign key referencing the primary key of the [AS_CORE].gradebook_grade table. No cascade delete because cleanup for associated data needs to be handled in the code.

    • gradebook_grade_pk1
  7. content_owner_fk7 (On Delete SetNull)
